ST Matthew Slater ''(1st team)'' | uniform = [[File:Patriots 16uniforms.png|250px]] | shortnavlink = Patriots seasons }} The [[2019 NFL season|2019 season]] was the [[New England Patriots]]' 50th in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), their 60th overall and their 20th under [[List of New England Patriots head coaches|head coach]] [[Bill Belichick]]. They entered the season as the defending [[Super Bowl]] champions, after winning [[Super Bowl LIII]], and as three-time defending [[American Football Conference|AFC]] champions. The Patriots won the [[AFC East]] for the 11th straight season, and improved on their 11–5 record from [[2018 New England Patriots season|the previous season]], but they were [[Upset (sports)|upset]] by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the Wild Card game, their first Wild Card game since the [[2009 New England Patriots season|2009 season]]. This marked the first time the Patriots lost a home postseason game since the [[2012–13 NFL playoffs#AFC: Baltimore Ravens 28, New England Patriots 13|2012 AFC Championship Game]] where they lost to the later Super Bowl champion Ravens 28–13, and the first time the Patriots failed to reach the [[AFC Championship Game]] since [[2010 New England Patriots season|2010]]. The Patriots were also the only NFL team that made the playoffs, and had a winning season, in every year of the 2010s decade. Catalyzed by their defense's historically dominant play, the Patriots started the season extremely well at 8–0 for the third time in franchise history, and early on there was conversation as to if they could repeat the undefeated [[2007 New England Patriots season|2007 regular season]]. However, their winning streak would soon end as a result of their Week 9 loss to the [[2019 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], which was also their first loss to the Ravens since the 2012 AFC Championship game. In Week 12, the Patriots set a new NFL record with their 17th consecutive 10-win season, surpassing the [[San Francisco 49ers]], who set the original record of 16 consecutive 10-win seasons from [[1983 San Francisco 49ers season|1983]]–[[1998 San Francisco 49ers season|1998]]. For the first time since [[2009 New England Patriots season|2009]], [[Rob Gronkowski]], the team's former starting [[tight end]], was not on the active roster as he announced his retirement on March 24, 2019.{{cite news |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/patriots-te-rob-gronkowski-announces-retirement-0ap3000001024012 |title=Patriots TE Rob Gronkowski announces retirement |first=Jeremy |last=Bergman |website=NFL.com |date=March 24, 2019 |access-date=March 24, 2019}} Also, for the first time since [[2010 New England Patriots season|2010]], the Patriots had a different kicker on the regular season roster as the struggling [[Stephen Gostkowski]] was placed on [[Injured reserve|IR]]; he was replaced by midseason signings [[Mike Nugent]],{{cite web|last=Ulrich|first=Logan|url=https://nfltraderumors.co/patriots-signing-k-mike-nugent/|title=Patr

The [[2005 NFL season|2005 season]] was the [[Green Bay Packers]]' 85th in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), their 87th overall and the sixth and final under [[List of Green Bay Packers head coaches|head coach]] [[Mike Sherman]]. It would be the first and only losing season the franchise would have involving quarterback [[Brett Favre]].

The Packers failed to improve their overall record of 10–6 from [[2004 Green Bay Packers season|2004]] and failed to make the playoffs for the first time since [[2000 Green Bay Packers season|2000]]. This would be their first losing season since [[1991 Green Bay Packers season|1991]]. As of the [[2025 NFL season|2025 season]], this is the only season since divisional realignment the Packers finished in last place in the NFC North.

The Packers suffered injuries to wide receivers [[Javon Walker]] and [[Robert Ferguson (American football)|Robert Ferguson]] and running backs [[Ahman Green]], [[Najeh Davenport]], [[Tony Fisher (American football)|Tony Fisher]], and [[Samkon Gado]]. As a result of the lackluster season, most of the team's coaches were fired, including head coach Mike Sherman.
